name: Acquired Monoclonal Immunoglobulin Light Chain-Associated Fanconi Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Light Chain Fanconi Syndrome Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of monoclonal immunoglobulin light chains in serum or urine
Evidence of proximal renal tubular dysfunction including aminoaciduria, glycosuria, phosphaturia, and bicarbonaturia
Clinical features consistent with Fanconi syndrome such as hypophosphatemia, metabolic acidosis, and osteomalacia
Exclusion of hereditary or other secondary causes of Fanconi syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of monoclonal light chains plus evidence of proximal tubular dysfunction and clinical features of Fanconi syndrome
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of inherited Fanconi syndrome and other causes of proximal tubulopathy.

pathognomonic.notes: Characterized by aminoaciduria, glycosuria, phosphaturia, and bicarbonaturia
searchTerms: renal tubule damage causing urine issues

pathognomonic.notes: Detected in serum or urine by immunofixation or electrophoresis
searchTerms: presence of abnormal antibody light chains

common.notes: Resulting from bicarbonate loss in urine
searchTerms: acid buildup in blood with normal gap
blood acidity due to metabolic causes

common.notes: Bone pain and fractures due to phosphate depletion

searchTerms: weakness related to salt or mineral problems

occasional.notes: Secondary to chronic disease or renal impairment

rare.notes: Kidney stones due to altered tubular handling

laboratory: Detection of monoclonal immunoglobulin light chains in serum or urine
Hypophosphatemia, hypokalemia, metabolic acidosis with normal anion gap
Aminoaciduria, glycosuria, phosphaturia, and bicarbonaturia on urinalysis
imaging: Bone demineralization and fractures on X-ray consistent with osteomalacia
genetic: No known genetic mutations; acquired condition associated with monoclonal gammopathy
other: Bone marrow biopsy may reveal plasma cell dyscrasia or monoclonal gammopathy

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of multiple myeloma with extensive bone lesions

redFlags: Presence of monoclonal protein indicating possible underlying plasma cell disorder
references: Leung N, et al. Light chain Fanconi syndrome: clinical and pathologic features. Kidney Int. 2012.
